summary: Catheterisation image processing requires segmentation models that are fast, accurate and explainable. While most of the existing studies usually focus on binary segmentation, there is a recent demand for simultaneous segmentation of multiple structures found in catheterization scenes. In this study, a dual-part MLBNet architecture is designed with multi-lateral encoder blocks and multi-head decoder branches for class-aware segmentation in cardiovascular catheterization scenes. Lateral branches in the encoder enables repeated feature extraction to learn diverse shared representations, while multiple decoder heads are used to introduce class-skewed branches that specialize in different structural properties in catheterization scenes. To analyze the performances of the dual-part MLBNet architecture, several multi-class segmentation angiogram data obtained during cardiovascular catheterization in phantom models, synthetic human-simulated aorta, and animal model are used for model training and evaluation. Results obtained showed the dual-part models could effectively separate guidewire, catheter, vessels and background pixels to their classes of memberships with high probability. The results demonstrate that all models were able to distinguish the dominant background class from foreground structures with high overall accuracy.

AI.tldr: A dual-part MLBNet for multi-class segmentation in catheterization scenes using multi-lateral encoder blocks and multi-head decoder branches for class-aware segmentation; evaluated on phantom, synthetic, and animal data with high accuracy in separating guidewire, catheter, vessels, and background.
AI.motivation: Need for fast, accurate, and explainable multi-structure segmentation in cardiovascular catheterization. Existing work emphasizes binary segmentation; growing demand for simultaneous, multi-structure segmentation in catheterization scenes.
AI.method: Proposed dual-part MLBNet with lateral encoder branches to enable repeated feature extraction and diverse shared representations; multiple decoder heads create class-skewed branches that specialize in different structural properties in catheterization scenes; trained/evaluated on multi-class angiogram data from phantom models, synthetic human-simulated aorta, and animal models.
AI.result: The dual-part models effectively separate guidewire, catheter, vessels, and background into their respective classes with high probability; all models distinguished the dominant background class from foreground structures with high overall accuracy.
AI.conclusion: The dual-part MLBNet demonstrates potential for effective class-aware multi-structure segmentation in cardiovascular catheterization scenes; results suggest good separation of multiple structures and robust background distinction, though quantitative baselines and broader clinical validation are needed to confirm real-world applicability.

title: REFINE: LLM Refinement over Budgeted Text-Attributed Graphs for Personalized Medical Concept Representation
comment: This paper has been accepted at the EMNLP 2026 main conference
summary: Learning rich medical concept representations is essential for EHR prediction. Text-attributed knowledge graphs (TKGs) provide a natural foundation by organizing heterogeneous medical relations together with textual semantics. However, most existing encoders process concepts uniformly across patients, despite the fact that a code's meaning and predictive value depend on patient-specific clinical context and trajectory. Learning patient-personalized concept representations from TKGs introduces two key challenges: (1) deciding how much KG context to incorporate for each observed code, and (2) aligning semantic information with the patient-specific relational structure. We propose REFINE, a KG-aware budgeted LLM graph refinement framework for patient-personalized medical concept encoding. Starting from a global TKG, REFINE constructs patient-specific temporal graphs. A sequential reinforcement learning policy selects a personalized KG expansion budget for each observed code. The resulting patient graph is processed by a heterogeneous GNN to capture relation-aware structural dependencies, while a frozen LLM uses graph-aware soft prompts to semantically refine concept representations. Experiments on MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV show that REFINE consistently improves diverse EHR backbones, outperforms strong baselines, and demonstrates robust gains across component ablation, KG selection, and data insufficiency.

AI.tldr: REFINE introduces patient-personalized, budgeted KG expansion for text-attributed knowledge graphs to improve EHR prediction by combining a sequential RL policy, a heterogeneous GNN, and a frozen LLM with graph-aware prompts, yielding robust gains on MIMIC-III/IV across backbones and data conditions.
AI.motivation: The meaning and predictive value of a code in EHRs depend on patient-specific context and trajectory; existing encoders apply uniform KG context without adaptation, limiting personalization and performance.
AI.method: From a global text-attributed KG, construct patient-specific temporal graphs; use a sequential RL policy to decide a personalized KG expansion budget per observed code; apply a heterogeneous GNN to capture relation-aware structure; employ a frozen LLM with graph-aware soft prompts to semantically refine concept representations; validate on MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV across various backbones and ablations.
AI.result: REFINE consistently improves diverse EHR backbones, outperforms strong baselines, and shows robust gains across component ablation studies, KG selection, and data-insufficiency scenarios.
AI.conclusion: Personalizing KG context via a budgeted, graph-aware framework that fuses structural learning (GNN) with semantic refinement (LLM prompts) enhances medical concept representations for EHR prediction and is robust across datasets and backbones.

title: HaptiNet: Networked Haptic Robots Enable Physical Co-presence in Geographically-Unconstrained Rehabilitation
summary: Cooperative rehabilitation enhances engagement, task performance, and social-motor interaction, yet it demands physical co-presence: users must transmit forces, coordinate movements, and infer intent through haptic contact. Telerehabilitation promises to expand access for patients constrained by distance, mobility, or clinical disparities, yet current techniques remain predominantly audiovisual while leaving users haptically and physically isolated. Here, we introduce HaptiNet, a networked haptic robotic system enabling physical co-presence for geographically distributed users via force-mediated interaction. Each robotic terminal features a low-inertia, long-stroke design with high force-feedback capacity, tailored for haptic rendering in upper-limb training. Building on these terminals, HaptiNet creates a distributed haptic network with an imitation-learning-based delay compensator, enabling users to physically perceive and coordinate with one another over distance. We validated HaptiNet in 284 healthy participants and 111 patients with neurological impairments across progressively realistic settings, including laboratory tests, cross-city deployments, and clinical applications. HaptiNet preserved task-level force rendering consistency across single-user and multi-user scenarios. Compared with solo and visual cooperative training, haptic cooperation improved task performance by 24% and 22%, respectively, while also boosting engagement and interpersonal motor synchrony. Across three intercity links totaling approximately 4,000 km, HaptiNet maintained stable haptic interaction among patients with neurological impairments, producing a 3.87-fold greater baseline-to-training score improvement and a 106% higher patient-applied effort over the solo condition.

AI.tldr: Networked haptic rehabilitation system HaptiNet enables physical co-presence between distributed users, delivering significant performance and engagement gains across real-world distances.
AI.motivation: Address the limitations of conventional telerehabilitation lacking haptic feedback and physical co-presence, which hamper task performance and social-motor interaction; extend access to rehabilitation across distance and clinical disparities.
AI.method: Design and validate HaptiNet: low-inertia, long-stroke haptic terminals with high force-feedback; distributed network with an imitation-learning–based delay compensator; experiments with 284 healthy participants and 111 neurological patients across lab tests, cross-city deployments, and clinical settings; compare haptic cooperation to solo and visual training; assess task-level force rendering, performance, engagement, interpersonal motor synchrony, and training score improvements over long-distance links (~4,000 km).
AI.result: HaptiNet preserves task-level force rendering across single-user and multi-user setups; haptic cooperation yields 24% performance gain vs solo and 22% vs visual training, plus increased engagement and interpersonal motor synchrony. Across three intercity links totaling ~4,000 km, system maintains stable interaction, achieving a 3.87-fold improvement in baseline-to-training score and a 106% higher patient-applied effort versus solo training.
AI.conclusion: HaptiNet demonstrates feasible, scalable distributed haptic rehabilitation with physical co-presence over distance, delivering substantive performance and engagement benefits and validating across laboratory, intercity, and clinical contexts.

title: Rethinking Indirect Prompt Injection as a Test-Time Search Problem
summary: We formulate indirect prompt injection as a test-time search over a task-dependent attack surface induced by the environment, user task, and injection task. To operationalize this formulation, we introduce an agentic attacker with a dedicated search harness that performs environment reconnaissance, structured reasoning over attack strategies, and adaptive evaluation using victim-agent feedback. Across heterogeneous tasks, we find that increasing attacker test-time compute improves vulnerability discovery and exploitation, while ablations show that explicit strategy management is important for avoiding redundant search and sustaining gains at larger budgets. These results suggest that agentic security evaluations should characterize both the attacker's search procedure and compute budget, rather than treating attack success as a budget-independent property of the victim. More broadly, our findings identify the attacker's adaptive search over the system attack surfaces as an important and underexplored security risk for tool-using agents.

AI.tldr: Indirect prompt injection is framed as a test-time search over an environment-induced attack surface. An agentic attacker with a search harness performs environment reconnaissance, strategic search reasoning, and adaptive evaluation using victim feedback. More compute improves vulnerability discovery; explicit strategy management reduces redundant search and sustains gains at large budgets. Security evaluations should account for attacker search procedures and budgets, highlighting adaptive exploration of system attack surfaces as a key risk for tool-using agents.
AI.motivation: To understand and quantify security risks posed by indirect prompt injection in AI agents and to propose evaluation practices that incorporate attacker search dynamics and compute budgets.
AI.method: Proposes an agentic attacker with a dedicated search harness that conducts environment reconnaissance, structured reasoning over attack strategies, and adaptive evaluation using victim-agent feedback. The framework is evaluated across heterogeneous tasks to study how test-time compute and strategy management affect vulnerability discovery and exploitation.
AI.result: Findings show that increasing attacker test-time compute enhances vulnerability discovery and exploitation. Ablations reveal explicit strategy management is important to avoid redundant search and to sustain performance at larger budgets.
AI.conclusion: The attacker’s adaptive search over system attack surfaces is a significant, underexplored security risk for tool-using agents. Security evaluations should characterize both the attacker’s search procedure and compute budget, rather than treating attack success as a budget-independent property of the victim.

title: Hidden In Plain Gaze: Gaze Representations as Privacy Controls for Utility and Re-identification Risk in XR
summary: Intelligent extended reality (XR) systems increasingly use eye and head tracking to infer user intent, task, and attention, but the same signals can also reveal biometric identity. We study whether gaze data representation choice can serve as a lightweight privacy control at feature extraction, before adding perturbation or formal privacy mechanisms. Using the egocentric HoloAssist dataset, we compare three gaze representations under matched model capacity: raw gaze, spatial attention heatmaps, and engineered eye-movement features. We evaluate each representation on action recognition as task utility and closed-set user re-identification as privacy leakage. Representation choice substantially changes the privacy-utility tradeoff. Engineered features retain roughly 85% of raw gaze's action-recognition accuracy while reducing re-identification by about an order of magnitude, to roughly four times the chance rate across 206 identities. This reduction attenuates rather than eliminates identity leakage, and the differences across representations show that abstraction alone does not guarantee privacy. Engineered features expose interpretable and auditable structure, giving designers a transparent privacy lever that complements mechanisms such as differential privacy.

AI.tldr: Gaze representation choice materially affects the privacy-utility tradeoff in XR: engineered eye-movement features can retain most task utility while substantially reducing biometric re-identification, offering a transparent privacy lever beyond raw perturbation.
AI.motivation: Identify lightweight privacy controls at feature extraction for gaze-based XR, balancing task performance with biometric leakage, using a simple pre-processing choice before applying further privacy mechanisms.
AI.method: Compare three gaze representations (raw gaze, spatial attention heatmaps, engineered eye-movement features) with matched model capacity on the egocentric HoloAssist dataset. Assess task utility via action recognition and privacy leakage via closed-set re-identification across 206 identities.
AI.result: Engineered features preserve ~85% of raw gaze action-recognition accuracy while reducing re-identification by about an order of magnitude, to roughly four times the chance level across 206 identities.
AI.conclusion: Abstraction in representation does not guarantee privacy. Engineered features provide interpretable, auditable structure and a transparent privacy lever that complements formal privacy mechanisms such as differential privacy.

title: Beyond a Universal Forecasting Selector: Demand-Conditioned Model Selection across Demand Patterns and Horizons
summary: Forecasting-model selection remains difficult in heterogeneous demand because the most suitable decision rule may vary with demand structure, data availability, and forecasting horizon. This study examines whether the selector itself should be treated as a context-dependent component of the forecasting process. Five selection mechanisms - RMSSE, ERA, OWA, CCG-AHSC, and CCG-AHSCD - are compared across 24 optimized forecasting models, nine datasets, three training-testing partitions, and horizons from 1 to 12 cycles. Selector performance is evaluated ex post using Global Relative Accuracy (GRA), statistical tests, and a best-attainable-model reference. No selector dominates across all conditions. CCG-AHSC and CCG-AHSCD are more competitive for Smooth demand and several Erratic configurations, whereas OWA and ERA perform better in Intermittent and Lumpy settings. Selector suitability also changes with historical data availability and horizon, supporting a context-dependent rather than universal approach to forecasting-model selection.

AI.tldr: No single selector dominates across all conditions; context-dependent performance of selectors depends on demand structure, data availability, and forecast horizon.
AI.motivation: Investigate whether the forecasting-model selector should be treated as a context-dependent component, given heterogeneity in demand and data.
AI.method: Compare five selection mechanisms (RMSSE, ERA, OWA, CCG-AHSC, CCG-AHSCD) across 24 optimized forecasting models, nine datasets, three training-testing partitions, and horizons from 1 to 12 cycles; evaluate ex post with Global Relative Accuracy (GRA), statistical tests, and a best-attainable-model reference.
AI.result: No selector dominates across all conditions. CCG-AHSC and CCG-AHSCD are more competitive for Smooth demand and several Erratic configurations; OWA and ERA perform better in Intermittent and Lumpy settings. Suitability of selectors changes with historical data availability and horizon.
AI.conclusion: Forecasting-model selection should be contextual rather than universal; tailor selector choice to the demand structure and data/horizon context.

title: CoLMIN: LLM-based Multi-Decision Path Negotiation for Cooperative Autonomous Driving
summary: Multi-vehicle cooperative autonomous driving enhances the safety and reliability of autonomous driving systems through information sharing among connected vehicles, demonstrating significant potential for improving traffic safety. LLM-based approaches leverage strong reasoning capabilities of LLMs to enable effective inter-vehicle negotiation and improve cooperative driving performance. However, driving decisions in complex traffic scenarios are inherently multi-solution in nature. As a result, existing negotiation-based methods often converge prematurely to suboptimal solutions, hindering consensus formation and limiting the practical deployment of cooperative autonomous driving systems. To address this challenge, we propose CoLMIN, the LLM-based multi-decision path negotiation framework for cooperative autonomous driving, achieving stable decision consensus through multi-decision path negotiation and reflective reasoning. To achieve stable and high-quality consensus in cooperative autonomous driving, CoLMIN consists of three key components: (i) an LLM-based Multi-Intent Negotiation module (LMin), which adopts a Negotiator-Evaluator paradigm and generates multiple candidate driving intentions for joint evaluation; (ii) an Evaluation-based Shallow Reflection Module (ESRM), which analyzes negotiation outcomes and provides feedback to guide subsequent negotiations, thereby accelerating consensus formation; and (iii) an LLM-based Deep Reflection Module (LDRM), which performs long-term reflection over negotiation histories to mitigate cognitive fixation and prevent the system from converging to suboptimal solutions. Experimental results in the CARLA simulation environment demonstrate that CoLMIN significantly outperforms existing methods in challenging interactive driving scenarios.

AI.tldr: A three-module LLM-based framework (LMin, ESRM, LDRM) for multi-decision path negotiation improves consensus quality in cooperative autonomous driving; demonstrated in CARLA.
AI.motivation: Driving in complex traffic scenarios presents multiple viable solutions; existing negotiation methods converge prematurely to suboptimal choices, hindering robust cooperative driving. LLMs offer enhanced reasoning for inter-vehicle negotiation to improve safety and performance.
AI.method: CoLMIN introduces: (i) LMin, an LLM-based Multi-Intent Negotiation module using a Negotiator-Evaluator paradigm to generate multiple candidate driving intentions for joint evaluation; (ii) ESRM, an Evaluation-based Shallow Reflection module that analyzes negotiation outcomes and provides feedback to guide subsequent negotiations; (iii) LDRM, an LLM-based Deep Reflection module that performs long-term reflection over negotiation histories to mitigate cognitive fixation and prevent suboptimal convergence. The framework integrates these components to achieve stable consensus, validated in CARLA simulations.
AI.result: Experimental results in CARLA demonstrate that CoLMIN significantly outperforms existing methods in challenging interactive driving scenarios, achieving more stable and higher-quality consensus.
AI.conclusion: LLM-based multi-decision path negotiation with reflective reasoning yields robust, scalable cooperative driving capable of avoiding premature suboptimal convergence; further work needed on real-world deployment, latency, and scalability.

title: BioSync: Transformer-Based Cross-Modal Fusion for a Multimodal Physiological Digital Biomarker
summary: Cardiac, neural, behavioral, and speech measurements from wearable and mobile devices provide partial, noise-sensitive views of physiological state. BioSync combines these measurements into the \textbf{BioSync Index (BSI)}, a continuous composite digital biomarker defined under the BEST framework. The model applies multi-head self-attention to modality tokens and adds a linear branch whose hypothesis class includes standard feature concatenation. This architecture is motivated by latent-variable measurement theory and by the possibility that joint observations contain information unavailable from individual modalities. We evaluated BioSync on two literature-informed synthetic cohorts: a four-modality cognitive-decline cohort using HRV, EEG, actigraphy, and speech, and a metabolic-autonomic cohort structured around the public AI-READI wearable schema. In the cognitive cohort, BioSync and concatenation obtained AUCs of 0.928 and 0.926, respectively. In the metabolic cohort, BioSync obtained accuracy/F1 of 0.764/0.766, compared with 0.756/0.758 for concatenation. The BSI correlated with latent severity in both cohorts ($r=0.91$ and $r=0.68$). A pure-attention ablation obtained cognitive-cohort AUC 0.911, locating the increase to 0.928 in the combined wide-and-deep architecture. With matched modality-dropout training, BioSync led concatenation at five of six cognitive-cohort corruption rates and at the highest metabolic-cohort rate. Its cognitive-cohort AUC was also higher than five published digital-biomarker reference values, although differences in datasets and tasks preclude a controlled benchmark claim. Comparison with single-modality, early-fusion, and late-fusion designs across six prespecified criteria identifies the model's computational properties; validation on real cohorts remains necessary.

AI.tldr: BioSync (BSI) is a multimodal digital biomarker built with a multi-head self-attention fusion of wearable modalities, showing competitive performance and robustness to modality dropout on synthetic cohorts, but real-world validation is pending.
AI.motivation: Wearable sensors provide partial, noisy views of physiological state. A unified, attention-based fusion that leverages latent-variable measurement theory can capture information unavailable from single modalities and yield a robust digital biomarker.
AI.method: BSI uses multi-head self-attention on modality tokens plus a linear branch that spans standard feature concatenation. Evaluated on two literature-informed synthetic cohorts: a cognitive-decline cohort with HRV, EEG, actigraphy, and speech; and a metabolic-autonomic cohort based on the AI-READI wearable schema. Included ablations (pure-attention), modality-dropout training, and comparisons to single-modality, early-fusion, and late-fusion baselines across six criteria; results include correlation with latent severity.
AI.result: Cognitive cohort: BioSync AUC 0.928 vs concatenation 0.926. Metabolic cohort: BioSync accuracy 0.764, F1 0.766 vs 0.756/0.758 for concatenation. BSI correlated with latent severity (r=0.91 cognitive, r=0.68 metabolic). Ablation: pure-attention AUC 0.911; wide-and-deep increases to 0.928. With modality-dropout training, BioSync surpassed concatenation at five of six cognitive corruption rates and at the highest metabolic rate. Cognitive AUC exceeded five published digital-biomarker references, though cross-dataset differences limit benchmarking; real-cohort validation remains necessary.
AI.conclusion: BioSync demonstrates promise as a robust, information-rich multimodal digital biomarker under the BEST framework, with superior performance in synthetic-cohort tests and resilience to modality corruption. However, validation on real cohorts is required, and its advantages are characterized across defined computational criteria rather than universal benchmarks.

title: An Evaluation Framework for Generating Multi-View Images of a Person in a Scene
summary: Recent generative image-editing Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) demonstrate impressive semantic editing capabilities but still struggle with spatially consistent camera angle changes. A primary bottleneck in training foundation models to execute free-form, promptable camera angle changes is the lack of specialized training data. While multi-view datasets exist for generic 3D environments and objects, there remains an absence of paired, multi-view datasets featuring human subjects at fixed locations in natural scenes, including frontal and side-profile views. Capturing such multi-camera data in unconstrained environments is logistically challenging and unscalable. In this paper, we first experiment with multiple state-of-the-art image editing models to create this data synthetically, but find that the outputs are frequently prone to hallucinations involving how much the subject's head turns relative to the background, often producing inconsistent environments. To address this issue, we propose the Head Scene Rotation Difference (HSRD) metric to quantitatively evaluate camera movements around a person. The proposed metric operates by decoupling camera movement from localized head pose manipulation. As demonstrated by the extensive experimentation, HSRD provides the pipeline necessary to evaluate 3D spatial parallax for a person in a scene, paving the way to reliably construct high-quality multi-view synthetic datasets.

AI.tldr: Introduces Head Scene Rotation Difference (HSRD), a metric to quantify camera movement around a person while decoupling head pose changes, enabling robust evaluation of 3D spatial parallax and construction of high-quality multi-view synthetic datasets for promptable camera-angle editing.
AI.motivation: To overcome the lack of specialized training data for free-form camera angle editing in diffusion-based image editors, particularly for humans in natural scenes, by enabling robust synthetic data evaluation and generation.
AI.method: Define HSRD to separate camera motion from head pose manipulation; validate via experiments using state-of-the-art image-editing models to synthesize multi-view data; assess with HSRD to estimate 3D parallax quality.
AI.result: HSRD provides a quantitative pipeline to evaluate camera movements around a person; experiments demonstrate its utility in assessing 3D spatial parallax and guiding the construction of higher-quality multi-view synthetic datasets.
AI.conclusion: HSRD enables reliable, scalable creation of multi-view datasets with consistent parallax for people in scenes, thereby facilitating training of foundation models for promptable camera-angle changes.

title: A Repeated-Measurement Study for Cultural Analytics of English Song Lyrics Using Five Large Language Models
summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to annotate cultural texts at scales that are impractical for human coders. However, before their outputs are treated as measurements of latent social constructs, it is necessary to establish whether those measurements are reliable. This study evaluates five LLMs as zero-shot annotators of four social constructs expressed in English song lyrics: self-esteem, self-control, seeking belonging, and seeking recognition. Using repeated annotations of a large lyric corpus, we examine three properties of LLM-based measurement: consistency across repeated runs, convergence across models, and transferability of consensus labels to supervised classification. The findings show that LLM-based measurement is not uniformly reliable across constructs. Self-esteem exhibits the strongest repeated-measurement reliability across models, while seeking recognition is generally less stable; self-control and seeking belonging show intermediate but model-dependent reliability. Downstream classification further indicates that consensus LLM labels contain learnable signal, although transferability does not itself establish construct validity. Repeated-measurement stability and cross-model convergence should therefore be reported before LLM annotations are treated as scalable measurements in cultural analytics.

AI.tldr: LLMs show variable reliability as zero-shot annotators for social constructs in lyrics; self-esteem most reliable, seeking recognition least; consensus labels have signal but do not guarantee validity; emphasize stability and cross-model convergence before scalable annotations.
AI.motivation: To assess whether LLM-based annotations of social constructs in cultural texts can be treated as reliable measurements, by examining repeatability, model convergence, and transferability to supervised tasks.
AI.method: Five LLMs used as zero-shot annotators for four constructs (self-esteem, self-control, seeking belonging, seeking recognition) in English song lyrics. Repeated annotations on a large lyric corpus to evaluate (a) consistency across repeated runs, (b) convergence across models, and (c) transferability of consensus labels to downstream supervised classification.
AI.result: Reliability is construct-dependent: self-esteem shows strongest repeated-measurement reliability; seeking recognition least stable; self-control and seeking belonging intermediate but model-dependent. Consensus LLM labels carry learnable signal for classification, but cross-model convergence and transferability do not by themselves establish construct validity.
AI.conclusion: Report repeated-measurement stability and cross-model convergence prior to treating LLM annotations as scalable measurements in cultural analytics; acknowledge that transferability to supervised tasks does not equal construct validity.

title: Strict Modes Everywhere - Bringing Order Into Dynamics of Mechanical Systems by a Potential Compatible With the Geodesic Flow
summary: Strict nonlinear normal modes provide very regular families of oscillations within conservative mechanical systems. However, a strict normal mode will generally be an isolated curve within the configuration space of the system. In this letter, we design a potential that will densely fill the configuration space with strict normal modes such that each configuration belongs to one mode and each mode passes through a common point, the equilibrium. As the potential can be realized by (nonlinear) elastic elements it can be used to execute a variety of periodic trajectories very efficiently. Most of the required torques will come from the elastic elements in the system and not from the actuators. We also design a controller stabilizing the system to a desired target mode and a controller performing swing-up and compensating dissipated energy. Finally, we showcase the approach for a two DoF manipulator. The experiments show that the approach performed well for the example system.

AI.tldr: Proposes designing a potential to densely fill configuration space with strict nonlinear normal modes (sNNMs) sharing a common equilibrium, enabling energy-efficient, actuator-light periodic trajectories; validated on a 2-DoF manipulator with stabilizing and swing-up controllers.
AI.motivation: Address the isolation of strict nonlinear normal modes by creating a dense foliation of the configuration space with sNNMs, using nonlinear elastic elements to realize the required torques.
AI.method: Construct a potential realized by nonlinear elastic elements that yields a dense set of sNNMs passing through the equilibrium; develop controllers to stabilize a target mode and to perform swing-up and energy dissipation compensation; demonstrate on a two-degree-of-freedom manipulator.
AI.result: Experimental results show good performance for the 2-DoF manipulator example.
AI.conclusion: The approach offers a practical pathway to realize dense families of periodic motions in conservative mechanical systems with mostly passive elastic action, improving efficiency and controllability.

title: What Does Multi-Harness RL Learn? Credit Assignment and Portability in Coding Agents
summary: Agent reinforcement learning (RL) increasingly runs through full execution harnesses, and a multi-harness recipe mixes two choices: exposing the policy to several harnesses, and comparing their rewards inside one relative-advantage group. We isolate the second choice in repository-level coding. From one Qwen3-8B supervised warm start we replay the same frozen task-harness records from Aider, OpenHands, Qwen Code, and SWE-agent, with the same number of updates, under two rules for group-relative policy optimization (GRPO), Within (one group per task-harness pair) and Cross (harnesses pooled within a task), and score every checkpoint with a sealed SWE-bench Verified oracle on four source harnesses and a minimal harness held out of training. The evaluation harness is the dominant variable: across 24,000 sealed evaluations it moves the mean solve rate from 2.14\% to 9.27\%, a factor of 4.3, where the training recipe moves it by 1.16. The grouping rule is not. On the held-out harness, Cross minus Within is +0.25 pp, 95\% confidence interval [-0.48, +1.02], at eight attempts per task, and +0.16 [-0.41, +0.72] pooled over three training seeds whose individual estimates change sign. Each rule's own seed range, 0.42 to 0.45 pp, exceeds the difference between them. Both rules place their largest gains on the same source harness. The pooled advantage carries the harness: an out-of-fold classifier recovers the generating harness from Cross's advantage +4.48 pp above the shuffled-label baseline and from Within's not at all, and the two rules still reach the same held-out score and action distribution inside each harness. Re-collecting half the training data on-policy does not change this. Cross-harness credit yields configuration adaptation and no more portable capability than within-harness credit. Multi-harness RL reports should state the grouping boundary and test under an unseen harness.

AI.tldr: Grouping choice (Within vs Cross) in multi-harness RL shows little held-out portability; evaluation harness dominates performance; cross-harness credit yields harness-specific adaptation with no extra transferability; report grouping boundary and test on unseen harness.
AI.motivation: Isolate the impact of the grouping boundary in group-relative policy optimization (GRPO) for multi-harness RL by controlling data replay and measuring across unseen harnesses with a sealed oracle.
AI.method: Replay the same frozen task-harness records from multiple sources (Aider, OpenHands, Qwen Code, SWE-agent) with identical update counts. Apply two GRPO rules: Within (one group per task-harness pair) and Cross (harnesses pooled per task). Evaluate every checkpoint with a sealed SWE-bench oracle on four source harnesses plus a held-out minimal harness. Analyze 24k evaluations, inspect held-out performance, seed variability, and harness recoverability via an out-of-fold classifier."
AI.result: The evaluation harness dominates performance: mean solve rate increases from 2.14% to 9.27% (factor 4.3) across 24k evaluations; training recipe accounts for only 1.16 percentage points. The grouping rule (Within vs Cross) does not yield a robust advantage: Cross minus Within is +0.25 percentage points (95% CI [-0.48, +1.02]) at eight attempts per task, and +0.16 pp (CI [-0.41, +0.72]) when pooled over three seeds, with seed-specific gains (0.42–0.45 pp) exceeding the inter-rule difference. Both rules gain most on the same source harness. An out-of-fold classifier recovers the generating harness under Cross (+4.48 pp over shuffled baseline) but not under Within, yet both rules achieve the same held-out score and action distribution within each harness. Re-collecting half of the training data on-policy does not alter the results. Conclusion: Cross-harness credit yields configuration adaptation but no greater portability than Within. Multi-harness RL results should report the grouping boundary and test under unseen harnesses to avoid overstating cross-harness transfer."
AI.conclusion: Portability claims for multi-harness RL should be grounded in held-out, unseen harness evaluations and explicit grouping boundaries. The apparent gains from cross-harness credit are harness-specific rather than portable; report both the boundary and unseen-harness tests to provide a fair assessment of GRPO methods.

title: Importance-Aware Low-Rank Distillation of Diffusion Transformers
summary:
Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) have emerged as a dominant architecture for high-quality text-to-image generation, yet their scale poses challenges for efficient deployment. While truncated singular value decomposition (SVD) is a principled tool for parameter reduction, evidence from large language models (LLMs) suggests that naive low-rank approximation can cause catastrophic failure. In contrast, we find that truncated SVD in DiTs produces smooth degradation even under substantial global compression, with redundancy distributed across projection matrices throughout the whole network rather than concentrated in a few transformer blocks. Building on these insights, we introduce SVDtrunc, a two-step block-level compression scheme, first allocating ranks across blocks and compressing the least important ones via truncated SVD under a global parameter budget, and then fine-tuning all blocks with modular knowledge distillation and a rectified-flow objective. We apply SVDtrunc to FLUX.dev across compression levels ranging from 40-90% of the original parameter count. Across three benchmarks, GenEval, HPSv2, and DPG, we outperform all competing approaches. Notably, and in contrast to prior work, we retain near-full performance at 68% and remain competitive even at 57% of the original parameter budget. Furthermore, we show that SVDtrunc complements step distillation and achieves strong results even without fine-tuning, positioning it as a practical continuation of efficiency improvements beyond diffusion step reduction for large-scale generative models.
  Project page: https://vislearn.github.io/SVDtrunc/

AI.tldr: A two-step block-level SVD-based compression (SVDtrunc) for diffusion transformers (DiTs) that allocates per-block ranks under a global budget, followed by modular knowledge distillation and rectified-flow fine-tuning, enabling 40-90% parameter reduction with smooth degradation and strong performance on GenEval, HPSv2, and DPG, including near-full performance at 68% budget and competitiveness at 57% without reliance on diffusion-step reduction alone.
AI.motivation: Diffusion transformers are large and hard to deploy efficiently. While SVD-based compression is risky in large models (potential catastrophic degradation), the authors investigate structured, block-level truncated SVD in DiTs to understand redundancy distribution and enable principled parameter reduction without severe performance loss.
AI.method: Two-step block-level compression (SVDtrunc): first allocate ranks across transformer blocks under a global parameter budget and compress the least important blocks via truncated SVD; then fine-tune all blocks with modular knowledge distillation and a rectified-flow objective. Applied to FLUX.dev with 40–90% parameter budgets; evaluated on GenEval, HPSv2, DPG.
AI.result: SVDtrunc yields superior performance compared to competing methods across three benchmarks, maintaining near-full performance at a 68% parameter budget and remaining competitive at 57%. It also demonstrates strong performance even without fine-tuning and complements step distillation.
AI.conclusion: SVDtrunc provides a practical, scalable pathway for compressing diffusion transformers beyond merely reducing diffusion steps. The distribution of redundancy across blocks and the proposed two-step compression with distillation/objective enables substantial parameter reduction with minimal loss, making large DiTs more deployable.

title: Conformity Breaks Conformal Prediction
summary: A conformal certificate can be valid when an LLM answers alone and invalid when the same LLM sees peers that unanimously assert a wrong answer. The question is unchanged; the model's score for the correct answer changes. We call this a score-mechanism shift: clean calibration certifies how the model scores answers alone, but not how it scores them under peer pressure. We show that this shift silently breaks conformal prediction in multi-agent LLM systems. Across open-weight models and multiple-choice QA tasks, coverage falls from a calibrated 90% to 74% under unanimous-wrong peers at the standard alpha = 0.10 operating point. The average hides a sharper failure: by targeting the low-confidence items the certificate still covers, an attacker nearly halves coverage on that subgroup, from 87% to 47%, while the monitored average remains much higher. The failure also reaches the decision layer: a system that should escalate when uncertain can instead become confident enough to act on the attacker's wrong answer. Standard conformal fixes do not solve the problem, because the question distribution has not changed; the model's scoring behavior has.

AI.tldr: Score-mechanism shift breaks conformal prediction in multi-agent LLM systems; peer pressure changes model scoring, reducing coverage and defeating standard fixes.
AI.motivation: Investigate whether calibration learned on a single model generalizes when models operate under peer influence and responses are aggregated in multi-agent settings.
AI.method: Empirical study across open-weight LLMs and multiple-choice QA tasks, introducing unanimous-wrong peer responses; evaluate conformal coverage at alpha=0.10; analyze subgroup sensitivity and escalation behavior; assess standard conformal remedies.
AI.result: Coverage falls from ~90% (calibrated when alone) to 74% under unanimous-wrong peers; targeted low-confidence items see coverage drop from 87% to 47%; escalation can be misled by the attack; conventional conformal fixes fail because the question distribution remains unchanged while scoring dynamics shift.
AI.conclusion: Conformal guarantees deteriorate under score-mechanism shifts in multi-agent settings; robust calibration requires strategies that account for peer influence and dynamic scoring rather than relying on single-agent calibration.

title: Coupled Control and Wireless World Models for Resilient Remote Robotic Control
comment: 13 pages, 13 figures. Submitted to IEEE Internet of Things Journal
summary: Remote robotic systems operating over wireless networks must maintain reliable control despite limited communication resources, changing channel conditions, and environmental disturbances.However, continuously transmitting high-dimensional sensory observations, such as camera images, increases communication overhead and energy consumption while reducing robustness under unreliable connectivity.To address these challenges, this paper proposes a resilient communication-aware remote robotic control framework based on coupled control and wireless Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) world models that jointly capture robot dynamics and wireless channel evolution from visual observations and a combination of raw and structured radio frequency (RF) representations based on spectrograms and Persistence Images(PIs).The learned latent representations enable predictive communication scheduling by jointly forecasting future robot states and wireless conditions, thereby reducing unnecessary uplink transmissions while maintaining reliable control performance.Furthermore, an adaptive resilience mechanism detects latent prediction discrepancies and efficiently adapts perception embeddings to accommodate wireless and visual environmental changes without retraining the complete control policy.The proposed framework is evaluated in a synchronized Gazebo-Robot Operating System (ROS)-Sionna robot-wireless simulation environment under diverse wireless propagation and perception perturbations.Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in communication efficiency, robustness, and resilience while maintaining navigation performance compared with conventional Proportional Integral Derivative (PID), model-free Deep Q-Network (DQN), and predictive approaches based on Vision Transformers(ViTs).

AI.tldr: A framework that jointly models robot dynamics and wireless channel evolution to enable predictive, communication-aware control with adaptive resilience, reducing uplink transmissions while maintaining navigation performance.
AI.motivation: To address the dual challenge of limited communication resources and unreliable wireless channels in remote robotic control, by integrating perception, dynamics, and channel evolution into a unified predictive representation.
AI.method: Coupled control and wireless Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) world models learn latent representations from visual inputs and mixed RF representations (spectrograms and Persistence Images). These embeddings forecast future robot states and wireless conditions to schedule communications and reduce uplink transmissions. An adaptive resilience mechanism adjusts perception embeddings in response to prediction discrepancies without retraining the entire control policy. Evaluation uses a Gazebo-ROS-Sionna synchronized simulation with varied wireless and perceptual perturbations.
AI.result: Significant gains in communication efficiency, robustness, and resilience while maintaining navigation performance. Outperforms conventional PID, model-free DQN, and ViT-based predictive approaches under diverse perturbations.
AI.conclusion: Joint dynamics-channel models with predictive communication and adaptive embedding resilience can reliably support remote robotic control over unreliable wireless links, balancing transmission cost and control quality; the framework demonstrates practical viability in high-fidelity simulation.

title: MaxKernel: Agentic Kernel Generation for TPUs
summary: Designing and authoring high-performance custom kernels for accelerators is a complex task that requires deep hardware-level expertise. Large Language Models (LLM) can be leveraged together with real-time compiler feedback to build agentic systems for kernel generation. In this work, we present MaxKernel, a multi-agent system that implements three distinct paradigms for TPU kernel development: (1) a Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) agent for collaborative, step-by-step design; (2) an Autonomous (Auto) agent that executes a fully automated, metric/trace-driven optimization loop; and (3) a Graph-Based Autonomous Search that scales the Auto agent for global exploration of the design space. All three paradigms leverage a shared pool of specialized sub-agents to handle planning, implementation, self-debugging, testing, and hardware profiling. We evaluate MaxKernel on JaxBench, a comprehensive suite of 50 diverse kernel tasks for TPUs, alongside complex, real-world workloads from state-of-the-art open-source models. We demonstrate that MaxKernel consistently generates highly optimized implementations, matching expert hand-tuned baselines and delivering significant performance across the benchmark. Our agent is open-sourced and available https://github.com/AI-Hypercomputer/accelerator-agents/tree/main/MaxKernel.

AI.tldr: MaxKernel is a multi-agent framework enabling TPU kernel design via HITL, autonomous, and graph-based search paradigms, achieving near-expert performance on JaxBench and real workloads; open-sourced.
AI.motivation: Automate high-performance accelerator kernel development by leveraging LLMs and real-time compiler feedback to reduce reliance on deep hardware expertise while exploring design space.
AI.method: Three paradigms (HITL, Auto, Graph-based Auto) with a shared pool of sub-agents (planning, implementation, self-debugging, testing, profiling); evaluation on JaxBench (50 kernels) plus real-world models; open-source repository.
AI.result: Consistently generates highly optimized implementations matching expert hand-tuned baselines and delivers significant performance gains across the benchmark.
AI.conclusion: Demonstrates feasibility of agentic kernel generation for accelerators; open-source release encourages adoption and further research.

title: ReaDiT Guidance: Control for Image and Video Generation using Diffusion Transformer Features
summary: We present DiT Readout (ReaDiT) Guidance, a lightweight framework for controlling generation with Diffusion Transformer (DiT) models via their internal feature representations. ReaDiT Guidance uses features from a single DiT block to steer the generative process according to spatial targets - like depth, pose, or edge maps - provided at test time. Furthermore, since modern text-to-video models are largely built on DiT backbones, ReaDiT Guidance naturally extends to video generation, enabling camera and motion control. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves competitive or improved results compared to existing feature-based and off-the-shelf adapter-based approaches while requiring fewer parameters.

AI.tldr: DiT Readout (ReaDiT) Guidance provides a lightweight, feature-based method to steer diffusion transformer generation using internal DiT features, enabling spatial control (depth/pose/edges) at test time and extending naturally to video with improved parameter efficiency.
AI.motivation: To enable controllable diffusion-based generation with minimal parameter overhead by leveraging internal representations of Diffusion Transformer (DiT) blocks, addressing the inefficiency of existing feature-based and adapter-based control methods.
AI.method: Utilize features from a single DiT block as guidance to steer the generative process towards specified spatial targets supplied at test time (e.g., depth maps, poses, edge maps). Extend this approach to video generation leveraging DiT backbones, leveraging their pre-existing video capabilities. Compare against existing feature-based and adapter-based baselines.
AI.result: Achieves competitive or superior results with fewer parameters compared to existing feature-based and adapter-based methods for both image and video generation with spatial control.
AI.conclusion: ReaDiT Guidance offers a lightweight, effective method for controllable diffusion-based generation by exploiting internal DiT features, scalable to video tasks with reduced model complexity.

title: When Load-Balancing Goes Too Far: Expert Pruning in Over-Dispersed Mixture-of-Experts Models
summary: Expert pruning reduces the memory and serving cost of Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models by removing low-importance experts identified by the router, assuming router probabilities provide a reliable importance signal. We observe that this assumption breaks down under over-dispersed routing, a regime associated with aggressive load-balancing during training, in which tokens are distributed nearly uniformly across experts and importance signals collapse. In this regime, perplexity does not predict downstream task accuracy: on gpt-oss-20B, the lowest-perplexity pruning configuration yields the worst mathematical reasoning, while the highest-perplexity configuration preserves it. This does not occur under standard routing (e.g., Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct), where perplexity and accuracy degrade together. Pruning under over-dispersed routing also exposes a capability trade-off in which no single scoring metric dominates: activation-aware scoring preserves mathematical reasoning but severely degrades knowledge-intensive science (an 18-point gap on GPQA), whereas frequency-based scoring exhibits the reverse. We propose Minimax Expert Score Allocation (MESA), a domain-aware method that iteratively boosts importance scores for experts serving whichever domain is currently worst-affected, minimizing worst-case domain degradation rather than average accuracy. At 25% expert pruning MESA achieves the smallest worst-case degradation across domains, outperforming activation-aware baselines on 7 of 11 benchmarks at a correspondingly reduced memory footprint, and it generalizes to gpt-oss-120B, Gemma-4-26B-A4B, and OLMoE-1B-7B. Our results indicate that over-dispersed routing is a qualitatively distinct pruning regime in which standard assumptions fail, and that recognizing it is a prerequisite for principled expert pruning of load-balanced MoE models.

AI.tldr: Under over-dispersed routing, router-based importance signals fail for pruning MoE models; the proposed MESA method mitigates worst-case domain degradation and yields robust pruning across models, outperforming baselines at 25% pruning.
AI.motivation: To reduce memory and serving costs of Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) by pruning low-importance experts using router-derived signals. However, aggressive load-balancing induces over-dispersed routing where router probabilities lose predictive power for downstream performance, invalidating conventional pruning heuristics.
AI.method: Identify that over-dispersed routing breaks standard pruning assumptions. Introduce Minimax Expert Score Allocation (MESA), a domain-aware, iterative method that boosts expert importance scores for the domain currently worst-affected, aiming to minimize the worst-case degradation across domains. Evaluate at 25% pruning across multiple models (gpt-oss-20B, gpt-oss-120B, Gemma-4-26B-A4B, OLMoE-1B-7B) and compare to activation-aware and frequency-based baselines.
AI.result: MESA achieves the smallest worst-case degradation across domains at 25% pruning, outperforming activation-aware baselines on 7 of 11 benchmarks, with a reduced memory footprint. It generalizes to additional models (gpt-oss-120B, Gemma-4-26B-A4B, OLMoE-1B-7B). The work shows over-dispersed routing is a qualitatively distinct pruning regime where standard assumptions fail, highlighting the need for principled, domain-aware pruning strategies.
AI.conclusion: Over-dispersed routing represents a distinct MoE pruning regime; conventional router-based pruning (e.g., using perplexity or single-score metrics) can mislead performance. A minimax, domain-aware approach like MESA is effective for robust pruning, offering improved worst-case domain performance and generalization across models.

title: Reasoning Without Inference Cost: Latent Semantic Scaffolding for Robot VLA Policies
summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models are trained by imitation and capture what action to take but not why; adding causal reasoning improves manipulation, but current methods pay for it at inference time - generating reasoning tokens or rolling out predicted future states at every step, a cost that compounds over long horizons. We ask whether this benefit can instead be captured during training and discarded before deployment. We introduce Latent Semantic Scaffolding (LSS), an auxiliary loss applied during human-demonstration pretraining that aligns a VLA's action-token representations to text embeddings of physical-reasoning rationales through a small projection head. The head is dropped at inference, leaving the unmodified base policy with zero added cost. Our central finding concerns alignment granularity: aligning each action token to the rationale of its own manipulation phase (Dense LSS) rather than to a single pooled episode-level embedding (Pooled LSS) yields representations that transfer markedly better to held-out tasks. Dense LSS attains both the best in-distribution success and the best transfer to tasks unseen during alignment, whereas pooled alignment over-specializes to the training task. A representational probe shows Dense LSS induces roughly twice the per-phase separability in the backbone, supporting that phase-local alignment is the operative mechanism.

AI.tldr: Proposes Latent Semantic Scaffolding (LSS): a training-time auxiliary loss aligning per-action token representations with text embeddings of physical-reasoning rationales (dense per-phase alignment) using a projection head that is discarded at inference; yields strong in-distribution and zero-runtime-cost transfer gains over pooled alignment.
AI.motivation: VLA models excel at imitation but lack causal reasoning; adding reasoning at inference incurs costly generation/rollouts. LSS seeks to capture benefits of reasoning during training, avoiding runtime overhead.
AI.method: Pretrain on human demonstrations with an auxiliary loss that projects action-token representations to rationale text embeddings. Dense LSS aligns each action token to its manipulation-phase rationale; Pooled LSS aligns to a single episode-level embedding. A small projection head enables this during training, which is discarded at inference.
AI.result: Dense LSS achieves the best in-distribution success and the best transfer to unseen tasks; Pooled LSS underperforms and over-specializes to the training task. A representational probe shows Dense LSS increases per-phase separability by about twofold in the backbone.
AI.conclusion: Phase-local alignment during training yields superior transfer and generalization without runtime costs; dense, phase-level alignment is the critical factor driving representational structure and performance.

title: Towards a universal language of concepts: A survey
comment: Originally completed as an M.S. capstone project at UCLA in 2022
summary: Humans can learn and generalize novel concepts from sparse data because they express knowledge in rich structural formats. In this paper, we propose that programs are a strong candidate for universal representation of concepts. We review computational models of concept learning that use programs as their concept representation and evaluate their contribution toward a universal representational language.

AI.tldr: Programs as universal representation for concepts; survey of program-based concept learning models.
AI.motivation: Humans generalize from sparse data by relying on rich structural representations. The authors argue that programs could serve as a universal language for concepts and knowledge.
AI.method: Review and synthesis of computational models that encode concepts as programs; evaluation framework toward a universal representational language.
AI.result: Provides a synthesis of existing program-based models and assesses their potential to form a universal representation; highlights strengths, limitations, and criteria for universality without reporting new empirical results.
AI.conclusion: Programming-based representations are a strong candidate for universal concept representation, but substantial work remains to establish true universality across domains.

title: Retinal OCTA Phenotyping with LLM Reporting for Alzheimer's Disease
comment: 4th IEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Blockchain, and Internet of Things, (AIBThings)
summary: Early identification of Alzheimer's disease (AD) remains challenging because established assessment methods can be costly, resource-intensive, or unsuitable for population-scale screening. Optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) provides non-invasive visualization of retinal microvasculature, but existing approaches often require diagnostic labels and provide limited measurement-level interpretation. We present an explainable OCTA pipeline that integrates annotation-aware vessel segmentation, layer-specific vascular biomarker extraction, label-free phenotyping, and measurement-grounded LLM reporting. Using 117 ROSE-1 images from 39 subjects, we apply annotation-matched segmentation models to superficial vascular complex (SVC), deep vascular complex (DVC), and combined SVC+DVC representations. The models achieve ROC-AUC values of 0.916-0.970 and Dice scores of 0.695-0.781. Six density and fractal-dimension biomarkers form subject-level profiles for exploratory clustering. Analysis of nine held-out subjects identifies an internally consistent lower-density, lower-fractal-dimension phenotype, although the absence of diagnostic labels prevents clinical interpretation. Reports generated using GPT, Gemini, and Llama are evaluated for measurement grounding, citation faithfulness, and diagnostic caution. Overall, the framework provides a transparent, non-diagnostic connection between retinal vascular measurements, exploratory phenotyping, and evidence-linked interpretation for Alzheimer's research.

AI.tldr: Explainable OCTA-based pipeline for Alzheimer's research that combines annotation-aware vessel segmentation, layer-specific vascular biomarkers, label-free phenotyping, and measurement-grounded LLM reporting on a small retinal image dataset; demonstrates high segmentation performance and a reproducible low-density, low-fractal phenotypic signature, with non-diagnostic, evidence-linked interpretation.
AI.motivation: To enable scalable, non-invasive, and interpretable retinal biomarkers for early Alzheimer's detection without relying on opaque diagnostic labels or clinician-dependent interpretation.
AI.method: Annotation-matched segmentation of superficial vascular complex (SVC) and deep vascular complex (DVC) from OCTA images, extraction of six vascular density/fractal biomarkers, subject-level profiling, exploratory clustering, and generation/evaluation of measurement-grounded reports using LLMs (GPT, Gemini, Llama) with assessment on citation faithfulness and diagnostic caution.
AI.result: ROC-AUC for segmentation: 0.916–0.970; Dice scores: 0.695–0.781. Identified six density/fractal biomarkers enabling subject-level phenotyping. On nine held-out subjects, found a consistent lower-density, lower-fractal-dimension phenotype. Reports show measurement grounding and evidence-linked interpretation, though no diagnostic labels.
AI.conclusion: The framework creates a transparent pipeline linking retinal vascular metrics to exploratory phenotypes and evidence-based reporting, offering a non-diagnostic pathway for Alzheimer's research while highlighting the need for diagnostic validation with labeled data.

title: On-board ML for Trace Gas detection in Imaging Spectroscopy data
comment: 2 pages; presented as a short (2 pages) paper at the IEEE HPEC26
summary: Data collected during aerial and spaceborne imaging spectroscopy campaigns enables the detection of transient events such as trace gas emissions. However, current processing pipelines depend on slow, on-the-ground processing, which delays the time to information of each detected event and prohibits immediate follow-up actions. During the Tokyo Field Campaign of March 2026, we explored on-board processing of Imaging Spectroscopy data from the equipped AVIRIS-5 sensor. Due to communication bottlenecks, full datacubes cannot be downlinked immediately during the flight. Instead we downlink the potential events predicted by our efficient and small machine learning model. We show the first on-board detection of methane point source emission with Imaging Spectroscopy data using Edge ML.

AI.tldr: On-board edge ML detects methane emissions from imaging spectroscopy data, enabling rapid event prediction and downlink during flights with limited bandwidth.
AI.motivation: Reduce time-to-information for transient trace-gas events by moving data processing onto aircraft/spaceborne platforms to overcome slow ground processing and downlink bottlenecks.
AI.method: Develop and test a compact on-board ML model that processes imaging spectroscopy datacubes from AVIRIS-5 to predict methane emission events; downlink only predicted events due to bandwidth constraints (Edge ML).
AI.result: First demonstration of on-board methane point-source detection using imaging spectroscopy with edge ML during the Tokyo Field Campaign, enabling downlink of event predictions instead of full datacubes.
AI.conclusion: Edge ML on-board processing is feasible and beneficial for rapid detection of transient gas emissions, reducing data latency and enabling timely follow-up actions.

title: ToPos: Automated Optimal Positioning on Topographic Manifolds using Constrained Geodesic Voronoi Decomposition
comment: ©2026 IEEE. Personal use of this material is permitted. Permission from IEEE must be obtained for all other uses, in any current or future media, including reprinting/republishing this material for advertising or promotional purposes, creating new collective works, for resale or redistribution to servers or lists, or reuse of any copyrighted component of this work in other works
summary:
Reliable autonomous mapping, environmental sampling, last-mile logistics, and infrastructure deployment depend on the optimal surface area-balanced distribution of Spatial Reference Sites (SRS). Conventional 2D Euclidean methods often fail in high-relief environments by neglecting topographic variations and physical obstructions. This leads to significant planimetric distortion, spatial clustering, and the placement of targets in inaccessible or shadowed regions, compromising both data integrity and operational safety. This paper introduces ToPos, an automated framework for TOPography-aware Optimal Sampling on topographic manifolds. We treat the terrain as a discrete 2-dimensional manifold embedded in 3D Euclidean space and replace standard flat-map distances with non-Euclidean geodesic distances that follow the actual surface geometry. The point distribution is formulated as an optimization problem using a Constrained Geodesic Voronoi Decomposition, solved via a Riemannian Nesterov Accelerated Gradient (NAG) engine. Our approach restricts target locations to a feasible "safe zone," accounting for non-traversable slopes, vegetation, environmental occlusions, etc. Through evaluations on non-convex sinusoidal manifolds, we show that ToPos mitigates planimetric distortion by utilizing geodesic metrics. This approach results in a $\sim$74% improvement in optimal surface area-balanced distribution, as measured by the coefficient of variation (CV) of the Voronoi cell areas. The framework is architected as a Geographic Information System (GIS)-ready micro-service to bolster the mentioned applications.
  Index Terms: Topographic Manifolds, Geodesic Voronoi Decomposition, Infrastructure Deployment, 3D Mapping, Spatial Sampling, and Non-Euclidean Optimization.

AI.tldr: ToPos: a geodesic, topology-aware sampling framework on 3D terrains that uses geodesic Voronoi decomposition and Riemannian optimization to achieve more uniform surface-area distribution within safe zones, outperforming 2D Euclidean approaches by reducing planimetric distortion.
AI.motivation: Conventional 2D planar sampling causes distortion and inaccessible target placements on high-relief terrains, jeopardizing data quality and operations. A topology-aware sampling method seeks accurate, safe, and uniformly distributed spatial reference sites on the actual surface.
AI.method: Model the terrain as a discrete 2D manifold embedded in 3D. Use geodesic distances, Constrained Geodesic Voronoi Decomposition, and solve with a Riemannian Nesterov Accelerated Gradient. Constrain placements to safe zones (non-traversable slopes, occlusions). Implement as a GIS-ready micro-service.
AI.result: Evaluations on non-convex sinusoidal manifolds show significant reduction in planimetric distortion and improved surface-area balance, achieving ~74% improvement in the CV of Voronoi cell areas.
AI.conclusion: ToPos provides a topology-aware, non-Euclidean sampling framework that improves distribution uniformity on terrain surfaces and is deployable as a GIS micro-service for mapping, sampling, and infrastructure deployment tasks.

title: Data-Driven Discovery of Composition-Dependent Constitutive Models for Hyperelasticity and Viscoelasticity of Digital Materials
comment: 40 pages including references, 9 figures in the main manuscript. Supplementary material is available upon request from the corresponding author
summary: Digital materials fabricated by multi-material 3D printing are designed as controlled mixtures of stiff and compliant constituents, yielding effective responses that span more than an order of magnitude in apparent stiffness and exhibit strongly nonlinear, composition-dependent, and rate-dependent dissipative behavior. Classical finite-strain viscoelastic models represent such behavior with closed-form strain energy functions for equilibrium and non-equilibrium stresses as well as evolution of internal variables, which may limit flexibility when a single constitutive model is expected to generalize across materials and loading rates. Here, we present a data-driven multi-material constitutive modeling framework that generalizes a formulation by Bergström and Boyce. The proposed framework retains the structure of the classical model, namely multiplicative kinematics, invariant-based strain-energy functions, and a scalar dissipative evolution law directed along the normalized nonequilibrium deviatoric stress. For the equilibrium branch, the data-driven discovery framework either directly predicts closed-form model parameters as functions of composition or automatically constructs a polyconvex strain-energy function using neural ordinary differential equations (NODEs). The nonequilibrium branch kinetics are learned similarly, either by directly identifying closed-form parameters across compositions or by using appropriately constrained artificial neural networks. Using multi-rate uniaxial compression data across multiple material compositions, we show that the proposed formulation captures rate-dependent stiffness and hysteresis across compositions while preserving thermodynamic consistency.

AI.tldr: Data-driven multi-material constitutive model extending Bergström and Boyce, using multiplicative kinematics, invariant-based energy, and neural ODEs to construct a polyconvex equilibrium energy and learn nonequilibrium dissipation; captures rate-dependent stiffness and hysteresis across material compositions while maintaining thermodynamic consistency.
AI.motivation: Provide a flexible, generalizable constitutive framework for multi-material 3D-printed composites whose apparent stiffness spans orders of magnitude and exhibits nonlinear, rate-dependent dissipation, overcoming limitations of fixed-form classical models.
AI.method: Retain Bergström–Boyce structure (multiplicative kinematics, invariant-based strain energy, scalar evolution law). For equilibrium, either map composition to closed-form parameters or synthesize a polyconvex energy via neural ODEs. For nonequilibrium kinetics, learn parameters across compositions or use constrained neural networks. Train on multi-rate uniaxial compression data across several compositions to ensure rate-dependent stiffness and hysteresis are captured with thermodynamic consistency.
AI.result: Demonstrated on multi-rate uniaxial compression data across compositions that the data-driven framework captures rate-dependent stiffness and hysteresis across compositions and preserves thermodynamic consistency, outperforming rigid fixed-form models in generalization across materials and loading rates.
AI.conclusion: A flexible, thermodynamically consistent constitutive framework that generalizes across material compositions and loading rates by embedding data-driven components within a classical Bergström–Boyce structure, enabling better predictive capability for multi-material systems.

title: Enhancing Multimodal Emotion Recognition via Multi-Feature Encoding and Attention-Based Fusion
comment: 15 pages, 6 figures, 6 tables. Pre-peer-review version. The final published version appears in ICONIP 2025, Lecture Notes in Computer Science, vol. 16312, pp. 142-157 (2026)
summary: Multimodal emotion recognition has attracted growing interest due to its importance in human-computer interaction, remote education, and healthcare. This paper proposes a novel multimodal emotion recognition framework that integrates rich audio and visual feature extraction with an attention-based fusion strategy. For audio, we extract three complementary feature types: semantic embeddings from Wav2Vec2, MFCC features, and statistical acoustic descriptors such as pitch, energy, and rhythm. These are aligned and fused via a BiLSTM to capture temporal dependencies. For video, we propose a ResNet50-BiLSTM architecture that combines deep residual learning and sequential modeling to extract expressive spatiotemporal features from facial sequences. To enhance multimodal synergy, we introduce a feature-level fusion mechanism based on multi-head attention, allowing the model to adaptively weigh contributions across modalities. Experiments conducted on the MELD and IEMOCAP datasets demonstrate that our model significantly outperforms baselines in both accuracy and robustness. Furthermore, ablation studies show that the attention-based fusion strategy significantly improves performance in unbalanced data settings. Our findings suggest that the proposed framework effectively captures diverse emotional cues from speech and visual expressions, and offers a practical and generalizable approach for real-world multimodal emotion recognition tasks.

AI.tldr: A multimodal emotion recognition framework integrating rich audio-visual features with an attention-based fusion strategy. Audio uses Wav2Vec2 embeddings, MFCCs, and acoustic descriptors aligned by BiLSTM; video uses ResNet50-BiLSTM; fusion via multi-head attention. Evaluated on MELD and IEMOCAP, it outperforms baselines and shows robustness, with ablations highlighting the advantage of attention fusion, especially on unbalanced data.
AI.motivation: To enhance emotion recognition by leveraging complementary audio and visual cues and a flexible fusion mechanism that can adaptively weigh modalities, aiming for higher accuracy and robustness in real-world scenarios.
AI.method: Audio branch extracts semantic embeddings from Wav2Vec2, MFCCs, and statistical descriptors (pitch, energy, rhythm); features are aligned and fused through a BiLSTM to capture temporal dependencies. Video branch uses ResNet50 followed by BiLSTM to model spatiotemporal cues from facial sequences. A multi-head attention-based feature-level fusion mechanism combines modalities with adaptive weighting. Evaluated on MELD and IEMOCAP datasets, with ablations to assess the fusion component.
AI.result: The proposed framework significantly outperforms baselines in accuracy and robustness on MELD and IEMOCAP. Ablation studies indicate that the attention-based fusion substantially improves performance in unbalanced data settings.
AI.conclusion: The framework effectively captures diverse emotional cues from speech and visual expressions and offers a practical, generalizable approach for real-world multimodal emotion recognition tasks.

title: Nested Inductive Bias Framework for SPD Manifold Learning
summary: In Geometric Deep Learning, inductive biases serve two primary functions: enforcing manifold constraints and embedding relational priors. Currently, representation learning on SPD manifolds frequently relies on pullback Euclidean metrics, such as the Log-Euclidean Metric, to satisfy the former. While computationally efficient in avoiding domain boundary violations, these metrics induce a flat geometry that may fail to capture the intrinsic relational priors of datasets. While metrics such as the Poincaré metric are widely utilized to induce domain-aligned relational priors, generalizing them from standard vector representations to the SPD manifold has remained a challenge. To bridge this gap, we introduce a Nested Inductive Bias framework that utilizes a two-stage diffeomorphic composition to formally pull back non-Euclidean target geometries onto the SPD manifold. This framework enables the construction of curvature-aligned Riemannian classifiers that simultaneously respect matrix constraints and the latent relational geometry of the data. Empirical evaluations on kinematic and signal processing benchmarks, together with synthetic experiments, demonstrate that deep manifold networks experience degradation in class separability unless the metric curvature aligns with the intrinsic data distribution. Furthermore, for standard vectorized architectures, we propose the Rational Conformal Metric (RCM), designed to establish state-of-the-art geometric robustness against outliers by bounding the representation space.

AI.tldr: Proposes Nested Inductive Bias framework to pull back non-Euclidean geometries onto SPD manifolds, enabling curvature-aligned Riemannian classifiers; introduces Rational Conformal Metric for vectorized architectures to improve robustness; shows curvature alignment is critical for class separability; empirical validation on kinematic, signal processing, and synthetic data.
AI.motivation: SPD-based representation learning often uses flat pullback Euclidean metrics (e.g., Log-Euclidean), which avoids boundary issues but fails to capture intrinsic relational priors. Generalizing non-Euclidean target geometries (e.g., Poincaré) to SPD has been challenging; bridging this gap can improve inductive biases.
AI.method: Two-stage diffeomorphic composition to pull back non-Euclidean target geometries (e.g., Poincaré) onto the SPD manifold, forming a Nested Inductive Bias framework. Build curvature-aligned Riemannian classifiers that respect positive semidefinite matrix constraints and latent relational geometry. For standard vector architectures, introduce Rational Conformal Metric (RCM) to bound representation space and improve outlier robustness.
AI.result: Deep manifold networks exhibit degraded class separability when metric curvature does not match data distribution; the proposed geometry alignment improves performance in kinematic and signal processing benchmarks and synthetic experiments. RCM achieves state-of-the-art geometric robustness against outliers by bounding representation space.
AI.conclusion: Aligning the curvature of the SPD geometry with data distribution is crucial for preserving discriminability in deep manifold networks. The Nested Inductive Bias framework plus RCM provide practical tools to enforce matrix constraints, embed relational priors, and enhance robustness in both SPD and vectorized settings.

title: A Schema Bounded Language Model for Refining Robot Policies Without Destabilizing Local Learning
summary: This paper addresses navigation by composite heterogeneous robots in a decentralized system when policy reasoning and local control operate at different update levels. In a NetLogo--Python implementation, three robots share motion dynamics but use different LLM backends. Each robot independently combines a large language model (LLM) policy agent, an Upper Confidence Bound (UCB) bandit, and a Double Deep Q-Network (Double DQN) controller; no central LLM generates team actions. LLM inference is confined to round-level policy generation and refinement rather than tick-level action selection. The robots perform cross-LLM communication through a shared round summary containing policies, outcomes, and learning feedback.
